text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, giving back some of last week's gains after hitting $137.20 on September 2nd. The decline comes despite oil prices holding firm—US crude at $91.48 and world oil at $96.02—suggesting the stock move reflects profit-taking rather than a broad energy selloff. Over the past week, the stock has been volatile, climbing sharply early in the week before pulling back the last two trading days.

The backdrop of escalating Iran-U.S. tensions and record gasoline prices—over $4 per gallon for Labor Day—had lifted energy stocks earlier this week, but today's pullback may reflect investors locking in gains after that rally, or caution ahead of the Labor Day holiday week when trading volumes often thin out.
